passages.original: De genere mortis illius mdlus Latinorum scripsit. Vera de Assumptione sententia. Sed nec invenitur apud Latinos aliquis tractatorum de ejus morte quidpiam aperte dixisse. Nam illum Evangelii versiculum quem Simeon dixit ad Domini Matrem , Et tuam ipsius animam pertransibit gladius (Luc. It, 55), beatae recordationis Ambrosius cum tractaret, ait : Nea historia nec litteræ docent, Mariam gladio vitam finisse. Hinc et Isidorus : Incertum est, inquit, per hoc dictum, utrum gladium spiritus, an gladium dixerit persecutionis. Sed quid de his de quibus loquor dicam;
passages.english: None of the Latins wrote about the manner of her death. The true view concerning the Assumption. But neither is any of the commentators among the Latins found to have said anything openly about her death. For when Ambrose of blessed memory was treating that verse of the Gospel which Simeon spoke to the Mother of the Lord, "And a sword will pierce through your own soul" (Luke 2:35), he says: "Neither history nor [any] writings teach that Mary ended her life by the sword." Hence Isidore also says: "It is uncertain from this saying whether he meant the sword of the spirit or the sword of persecution." But what am I to say about these [men] of whom I am speaking,
